subject: Planned maintenance: EU-North kernel & driver compatibility wave — June 20-21 (staggered)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: customers-eun@redwood.com, jane.summers@acmecloud.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T08:15:00+00:00
Subject: Planned maintenance: EU-North kernel & driver compatibility wave — June 20-21 (staggered)

Hi all,

Heads-up: we are scheduling a staggered maintenance window in EU-North to roll a coordinated kernel + driver compatibility update for our inference nodes. This is a pre-planned, validated change intended to improve stability and enable a newer driver build that reduces OOMs for long-running sessions.

Planned window
- Dates: 2027-06-20 22:00 UTC through 2027-06-21 06:00 UTC (staged across racks)
- Pattern: rolling, rack-by-rack restarts; each GPU host will be restarted once during the window
- Expected customer impact: short (approx. 1-7 minutes) disruption for active inferences on a restarted host. Connections will be reestablished; we will route traffic away before restart where possible.

Scope
- Affected regions: eu-north only
- Affected instance types: r6g.* and g5.* serving pools (pinned instances may experience truncated requests)

Mitigations in place
- Canary fleet (10% of capacity) will be updated first and validated for 6 hours
- Automatic fallback to previous driver variant if health checks fail
- Controlled batching and KV-cache preservation for compatible models

What we need from customers
- If you have hard blackout dates or long-running jobs during Jun 20-21, reply with the project tag or instance IDs and we will exclude those nodes from the first two phases of the roll.
- Please ensure your clients can reconnect (most SDKs already do) and let us know if you need a pre-change readiness call.

Attachments: eun-maintenance-runbook.pdf (runbook, checklist, rollback steps)

We will publish a status page update and send a final reminder 48h and 2h before the canary. If you prefer a one-off email to a point-contact, reply with the address.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Ops PM, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0123

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T14:30:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: EU-North kernel & driver compatibility wave — canary plan update

Dylan — quick update from the deployment side:

- We added a preflight firmware/driver compatibility check to the canary job that verifies kernel symbols and driver ABI before any restart. If the check fails, the host will be drained and moved to the post-rollback queue.
- Canary schedule: 2027-06-20 22:00 UTC (10% capacity) for 6 hours, then phased ramp at 30%/60%/100% with 90m verification windows between phases.
- Added a short-lived feature flag to route idle sessions away from nodes scheduled in the next 30 minutes.

Attached: canary-checklist.xlsx (checklist + verification steps).

Action items:
- Dev: please ensure the automatic fallback path (driver-variant selector) is enabled and tested in staging (ticket DEPLOY-1123).
- Hannah / Support: prepare targeted notice to ACME (use tags provided by Jane) and other customers with tagged instances.

Lauren
Director, Platform Deployments

I’ve attached scheduled-ids.csv with the host IDs and the current plan matrix (for support routing). On-call escalation for the window: +1-415-555-0909 (Ops Lead).

Attachments: scheduled-ids.csv

Dylan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: customers-eun@redwood.com, jane.summers@acmecloud.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T16:45:00+00:00
Subject: EU-North maintenance: completion & brief post-action summary (Jun 20-21)

Status: Completed — overall success with minor impact

Summary:
- Maintenance period: 2027-06-20 22:00 UTC through 2027-06-21 05:40 UTC
- Canary: completed successfully (validated 6h)
- Rollout: phased to 100% as planned

Customer impact observed:
- Most customers saw no perceptible disruption.
- Three customers experienced short spikes in error rates while particular hosts restarted: two hosts had extended restart times (~7 minutes) due to a delayed driver reload sequence. Affected customers were contacted directly (ACME included; Jane — we followed up per your request).

Root cause and actions:
- Root cause: a small subset of hosts had a firmware/driver sequence that caused the driver reload to block on a vendor kernel module; this was not caught by the initial compatibility check.
- Immediate remediation: manual restart and forced driver reload on the two hosts; we routed traffic away during remediation.
- Follow-ups: add a pre-boot module check in preflight (in addition to the symbol ABI check), extend canary verification window for the first vendor-family, and add an automated forced-reload fallback for that module family.

Artifacts and notes: attached postmortem-notes.pdf and incident-runbook.log.

If you saw an unresolved issue after the window, please reply to this thread or open a ticket with support and reference INC-20270621-EUN. We’ll prioritize any remaining follow-ups.

Thanks for your patience and the quick coordination — Lauren/Dev/Hannah did a great job with the canary and support notices.

Dylan Brooks
Sr. Ops PM, Redwood Inference
